The explicit trace/determinant and sign formulas yield necessary and sufficient strict Schur+admissibility conditions for LLR. The LRR starting coordinate numerator is strictly positive under both saddle inequalities, contradicting L admissibility whenever the return is Schur stable. The exact rational witness is checked by Fraction against all three state equations and positive Jury margins; finite checks do not substitute for universal algebraic proof.

originality.rationale: The direct 2024 two-saddle BCNF study examines mainly chaotic component bifurcations and stable periods 2/4; it does not state a complete strict Schur-attracting period-three classification. The fully read 2022 Fatoyinbo–Simpson synopsis indeed shows stable LLR at a=0.5,d=0.5 outside the required two-saddle set, and studies LRR at negative offset; neither establishes the complete all-Phi LLR criterion or the LRR obstruction. The 2014 Simpson work is a different codimension-three infinite-attractor construction. Standard word matrices/Jury inequalities are acknowledged. An unlocated equivalent general treatment remains a priority risk.
residual_risks: General symbolic-cycle methods make the classification approachable, and an exact equivalent may have been published under different notation.
Some wider BCNF papers were only available or used at abstract level; no claim of exhaustive literature coverage.
Source 2022/2023 already shows attracting LLR outside the two-saddle region, so novelty is specifically the strict all-Phi classification and rational witness, not existence of LLR cycles generally.

value.rationale: The two-saddle BCNF domain is selected precisely for complicated chaotic and low-period dynamics. A strict complete itinerary classification and explicit open attracting-three-cycle locus distinguish permissible periodic sinks from prohibited words in a mathematically natural full four-parameter region. This is more informative than one numerical example, an arbitrary parameter substitution, or reusing the already known attracting-LLR example outside Phi; it supplies exact decision inequalities and a structural opposite-word exclusion.
